headline: Online bullying is rising again, and AI-made fake images are a growing share of the reports.
score_reason: Pool 5; figures read in full from the relayed report; no change.
importance_line: AI-made fake images are a growing share of online bullying of children, which affects children first and then parents and schools, and the doubt is that these are figures from one organisation's reports, not a national count.
summary: RTL Nieuws reports, citing Offlimits, the expertise centre for online abuse, that online bullying reports rose to 955 between January and September 2026, more than the 860 received in all of 2025. AI-generated or manipulated images now make up 17.4% of those reports, up from 2% in 2024, and young people say peers use them to humiliate each other, and some of the images show teachers.
notes: Read in full on NL Times, which relays RTL Nieuws (which reported Offlimits' figures). RTL Nieuws article not fetched, so the NL Times page is the url; noted. Pool curator note: consumer and community impact.
